Source: docs/REVISTAS_PLAN.md §3.1-bis. Frozen here because the live case is
gone — the site now serves the 03.08–09.08 period, so a test that probed
vital.com.ar could never reproduce it again.
Every row is THE SAME FLYER re-exported: same URL, same period, same pages.
Only content-length/ETag/Last-Modified moved, which is exactly what the dedup
hash keys off — hence the pipeline saw five 'new editions' that were not.
The re-exports of 2026-08-05, measured read-only against production the same
day. Same PDF URL, same exact period as the stored issue — and size deltas of
1.26% and 3.37%, i.e. FAR past REUPLOAD_SIZE_TOLERANCE_PCT (0.5%). The size
rule let both through: 34 pages of vision were re-read and the curated rows
(118 + 14 approved items) were superseded. These are the cases the URL rule
Rosental on 2026-08-05: the same book read twice. Identical title, identical
144 page files and identical 80,401,900 bytes downloaded — only the HTTP
metadata of config.js moved, which the discovery hash used to include.
